title: Act on the Development of the Floriculture Industry and Promotion of Floral Culture
title_original: 화훼산업 발전 및 화훼문화 진흥에 관한 법률
full_text:
ACT ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE FLORICULTURE INDUSTRY AND PROMOTION OF FLORAL CULTURE

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the development of the national economy and improvement of the quality of life of the people by establishing a foundation for the development of the floriculture industry and promoting floral culture, by prescribing matters necessary for fostering and supporting the floriculture industry.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
1. "Flowers and ornamental plants" means plants cultivated for ornamental, processing, or other uses, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
2. "Floriculture industry" means an industry concerned with breeding, cultivation, processing, distribution, and sale of flowers and ornamental plants and the provision of related education and services.
3. "Floral culture" means tangible and intangible ways of life that have evolved and developed in relation to flowers and ornamental plants.

Article 3 (Duties of the State, Local Governments, etc.)
(1) The State and local governments shall establish and implement policies necessary for developing the floriculture industry and promoting floral culture. <Amended on April 22, 2025>
(2) The State, local governments, and public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions (hereinafter referred to as "public institutions") shall endeavor to promote the use of flowers and ornamental plants, including by expanding their purchases. <Newly Inserted on April 22, 2025>

Article 4 (Relationship to Other Acts)
Unless otherwise specially provided for in other Acts, matters concerning development of the floriculture industry and promotion of floral culture shall be governed by this Act.

CHAPTER II ESTABLISHMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF COMPREHENSIVE PLANS TO FOSTER THE FLORICULTURE INDUSTRY

Article 5 (Establishment and Implementation of Comprehensive Plans to Foster Floriculture Industry)
(1) Every five years, the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs shall establish and implement a comprehensive plan to foster the floriculture industry (hereinafter referred to as a "comprehensive plan") for the development of that industry and promotion of floral culture.
(2) A comprehensive plan shall include the following:
1. Basic objectives and implementation directions for fostering the floriculture industry and promoting floral culture;
2. Production and adjustment of supply and demand of flowers and ornamental plants;
3. Encouraging the use of flowers and ornamental plants in everyday life, promoting their use, and supporting distribution;
4. Surveys, research, technological development, and dissemination related to flowers and ornamental plants;
5. Development and dissemination of related education, training of professionals, and horticultural therapy programs;
6. Creation of floriculture industry promotion zones;
7. Support for exports and overseas market entry related to the floriculture industry;
8. Promotion of and support for floral culture;
9. Statistics and informatization concerning flowers and ornamental plants;
10. Other matters necessary to foster the floriculture industry and promote floral culture.
(3) Upon establishing a comprehensive plan under paragraph (1), the Minister shall notify the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayors, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Do Governors, and Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as "Mayors/Do Governors") thereof.
(4) Where deemed necessary to establish or amend a comprehensive plan, the Minister may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, Mayors/Do Governors, and relevant institutions or organizations to submit materials. The heads of relevant agencies and others receiving such requests shall comply unless there are justifiable grounds not to do so.
(5) Other matters necessary for establishment and implementation of a comprehensive plan shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Establishment and Implementation of Implementation Plans)
(1) Every five years, Mayors/Do Governors shall establish and implement an implementation plan (hereinafter referred to as an "implementation plan") to foster the floriculture industry and promote floral culture in accordance with the comprehensive plan.
(2) An implementation plan shall include:
1. The status of the local floriculture industry and floral culture;
2. The objectives, basic directions, and implementation directions for fostering the local floriculture industry and promoting floral culture;
3. Securing and providing financial resources for fostering the local floriculture industry and promoting floral culture;
4. Allocation of roles among local flower-related institutions;
5. Other matters a Mayor/Do Governor deems necessary for fostering the floriculture industry and promoting floral culture.
(3) Each Mayor/Do Governor shall submit annual implementation results under the implementation plan to the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs.
(4) Matters necessary for establishment and implementation of implementation plans, and other matters, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER III DEVELOPMENT OF FLORICULTURE INDUSTRY

Article 7 (Compilation of Statistics and Surveys of Actual Conditions)
(1) The Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs shall compile and manage statistics concerning the floriculture industry and conduct surveys of actual conditions to secure basic data necessary for establishment and implementation of policies to develop the floriculture industry and promote floral culture.
(2) Where necessary for compilation of statistics and surveys under paragraph (1), the Minister may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, local governments, public institutions, and floriculture-related institutions or organizations to provide materials. Persons receiving such requests shall comply unless there are justifiable grounds not to do so. <Amended on April 22, 2025>
(3) The Minister may establish and operate a comprehensive information management system for flowers and ornamental plants, based on statistics and survey results under paragraph (1), to provide information concerning their production, distribution, demand, etc. and systematically manage the status of the floriculture industry.
(4) The Minister may entrust specialized institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree with establishing and operating the system under paragraph (3) and provide necessary administrative and financial support.
(5) The frequency, methods, and scope of compilation of statistics and surveys, establishment and operation of the comprehensive information management system, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 8 (Promotion of Research and Technological Development)
(1) The Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs shall promote the following research and technological development for development of the floriculture industry and promotion of the use of flowers and ornamental plants:
1. Breeding of flower and ornamental plant varieties and enhancement of technologies for propagating seedlings and seeds;
2. Development of technologies to improve productivity and quality, including cultivation and quality management;
3. Development of various processed products using flowers and ornamental plants;
4. Promotion of dissemination of floriculture research results and technologies;
5. Other matters necessary for research and technological development related to the floriculture industry.
(2) To promote technological development in the floriculture industry, the Minister may support necessary expenses for persons undertaking research and technological development under paragraph (1) or commercializing the results.

Article 9 (Designation and Revocation of Floriculture Industry Promotion Zones)
(1) Upon application by a Mayor/Do Governor, the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs may designate as a floriculture industry promotion zone (hereinafter referred to as a "promotion zone") an area where flower and ornamental plant production is carried out on a significant scale and facilities for related production, distribution, sale, etc. are concentrated, to foster the local floriculture industry.
(2) The Minister and Mayors/Do Governors may provide necessary support, including installation and improvement of floriculture-related facilities, marketing, and publicity, to foster promotion zones designated under paragraph (1).
(3) The Minister may revoke designation of a promotion zone under paragraph (1) in any of the following cases:
1. Where designation was obtained by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where the purpose of designation cannot be achieved or is expected to become unattainable;
3. Where the promotion zone no longer meets the designation requirements;
4. Where another ground prescribed by Presidential Decree exists.
(4) Designation requirements, application and designation procedures, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 10 (Improvement of Production and Distribution Systems)
(1) The State and local governments may support installation of production infrastructure and other measures for stable production and quality improvement of flowers and ornamental plants.
(2) The State and local governments may implement policies necessary to improve distribution efficiency and expand and organize producers' organizations.

CHAPTER IV PROMOTION OF FLORAL CULTURE

Article 11 (Dedicated Agency for Promotion of Floral Culture)
(1) The Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs may designate a dedicated agency for promotion of floral culture (hereinafter referred to as a "dedicated agency") to systematically implement policies concerning promotion of floral culture.
(2) The Minister may support the expenses necessary for a dedicated agency to perform its duties.
(3) Where a designated dedicated agency falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Minister may revoke its designation or order suspension of all or part of its business for a period not exceeding six months, as prescribed by Presidential Decree: Provided, That the Minister shall revoke designation in the case under subparagraph 1:
1. Where designation was obtained by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where the dedicated agency no longer meets the requirements for designation;
3. Where the agency has not performed duties relating to promotion of floral culture for at least one year without justifiable grounds;
4. Where it has otherwise become manifestly inappropriate for the agency to perform duties as a dedicated agency.
(4) Procedures for designation and revocation of designation of dedicated agencies, and other necessary matters for their operation, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Development of Excellent Flower Shops)
(1) The Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs may select as excellent flower shops those shops equipped with facilities, specialized personnel, etc. necessary for quality management, to improve the quality of flowers and ornamental plants and protect consumers' interests.
(2) The Minister may provide excellent flower shops selected under paragraph (1) with support for marketing, quality management, related education, and publicity within budgetary limits.

Article 13 (Education and Training)
(1) The State and local governments may directly provide or entrust education and training for consumers, floriculture industry workers, etc. to disseminate and transfer flower-related knowledge and technology for development of the floriculture industry and promotion of floral culture.
(2) Where the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs entrusts education and training under paragraph (1), the Minister may support the necessary expenses within budgetary limits.

Article 14 (Labeling and Notification of Reused Floral Wreaths)
(1) A person who sells floral wreaths made using fresh flowers that have been reused (hereinafter referred to as "reused wreaths"), or who makes, stores, or displays them for sale, shall indicate that they are reused wreaths and notify consumers, distributors, etc. of that fact.
(2) The matters to be indicated, methods of labeling, and other necessary matters concerning reused wreaths under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 15 (Prohibition of False Labeling of Reused Wreaths, etc.)
A person required to label reused wreaths under Article 14 (1) (hereinafter referred to as a "person obliged to label reused wreaths") shall not engage in any of the following:
1. Falsely labeling a reused wreath or displaying a label likely to cause confusion;
2. Damaging or altering a label indicating that a wreath has been reused.

Article 16 (Investigation of Reused Wreath Labeling, etc.)
(1) The Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs or a Mayor/Do Governor may authorize relevant public officials to conduct investigations as prescribed by Presidential Decree to verify whether reused wreaths are labeled under Articles 14 and 15, the appropriateness of matters and methods of labeling, and any violations thereof.
(2) The Minister or a Mayor/Do Governor may have honorary inspectors for agricultural and fishery products under Article 104 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act provide guidance and publicity on labeling of reused wreaths and report violations, and may pay necessary expenses.

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 17 (Reports and Inspections)
(1) The Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs may order a dedicated agency to report on its duties or submit materials, or authorize subordinate public officials to enter the premises or inspect documents.
(2) Public officials conducting entry or inspections under paragraph (1) shall carry identification indicating their authority and present it to the relevant persons.

Article 18 (Delegation and Entrustment of Authority)
(1) The Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs may delegate part of the authority under this Act to Mayors/Do Governors, the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration, or heads of agencies affiliated with the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) A Mayor/Do Governor, Administrator of the Rural Development Administration, or head of an affiliated agency to whom authority has been delegated under paragraph (1) may, with approval of the Minister, further delegate part of that authority to the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu (meaning the head of an autonomous Gu; the same shall apply hereinafter) or to the head of an affiliated agency.
(3) The Minister may entrust part of the duties under this Act to heads of public institutions or relevant organizations as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 19 (Hearings)
Where the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs revokes the designation of a dedicated agency designated under Article 11, the Minister shall hold a hearing.

Article 20 (Persons Deemed Public Officials for Application of Penalty Provisions)
Officers and employees of institutions or organizations engaged in duties entrusted by the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs under Article 18 (3) shall be deemed public officials for the purposes of applying Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

CHAPTER VI PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 21 (Administrative Fines)
(1) An administrative fine not exceeding ten million won shall be imposed on any of the following persons:
1. A person who fails to label reused wreaths in violation of Article 14 (1);
2. A person who violates the labeling methods for reused wreaths under Article 14 (2);
3. A person obliged to label reused wreaths who falsely labels them or uses labels likely to cause confusion in violation of Article 15 (1);
4. A person obliged to label reused wreaths who damages or alters the labels in violation of Article 15 (2).
(2) An administrative fine not exceeding five million won shall be imposed on a person who fails to submit materials under Article 17 without justifiable grounds or submits false materials.
(3) Administrative fines under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, a Mayor/Do Governor, or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 16473, August 20, 2019>

This Act shall enter into force one year after the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 20925, April 22, 2025>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
